I found no dedicated Houston 311 dataset on data.houstontx.gov in these results. The public 311 data appears to be served from the city's ArcGIS REST server instead.

- **Where the data lives:** The city's GIS server hosts a 311 service requests layer, all publicly available service requests filed in the LAGAN are included in this dataset.
- **Update schedule:** The layer is refreshed monthly from the LAGAN system (Monthly update from Lagan).
- **Exclusions:** Animal-related requests are left out, since they are filed in the Chameleon system. The city suggests pairing this layer with a separate BARC location dataset for a full picture (this data set can be used in conjunction with PUBLIC_BARC_Location).
- **Access and limits:** The layer supports JSON, GeoJSON, and PBF queries, with a MaxRecordCount: 2000 cap per request. Coordinates use a Texas South Central State Plane projection in feet, which matters if you map the points.
- **Portal context:** The city's open data portal at data.houstontx.gov is a CKAN site with 83 listed datasets in one snapshot. The portal pages I saw listed other datasets, such as Checkbook, Payroll, and Budget, but not a 311 dataset.

Check the portal's search directly for a 311 CSV download, since these results may not show everything it hosts.

The OpenDataPhilly dataset is the City of Philadelphia's record of Philly311 requests, with some access caveats.

- **Scope:** It represents all service and information requests since December 8th, 2014 submitted to Philly311 via the 311 mobile application, calls, walk-ins, emails, the 311 website or social media. The dataset includes two main data points – requests for services or information.
- **Size and access:** It is a very large dataset. Unless you are comfortable working with APIs, the site recommends using the visualization to explore the data. The API is served through Carto's SQL API. Because the dataset is large, CSV and SHP files might give an error when you try to download them. If you can't use the API and have trouble downloading the full files, the data has been split up by year.
- **Currency:** A harvested data.gov copy shows a metadata update date of April 13, 2026, and a Data Last Modified field of R/P1D, which suggests a daily refresh interval. I didn't confirm this against the OpenDataPhilly page itself.
- **Terms:** The City makes no representation about the accuracy of any specific information in this data, which is provided "as is."
- **Third-party note (less authoritative):** An Apify actor describes the same records as an ArcGIS layer named PUBLIC_CASES_FC, with requests ranging from 2014-01-01 to the current day. It also reports counts that change as the layer is edited, so treat its figures as a snapshot rather than official numbers.

content.content:
**Name:** MyLA311 Service Request Data 2016

**Description:** Service request data from MyLA311 for 2016, including requests from 311, call centers, email, mobile apps, the website, and other sources.

**Update frequency:** Weekly, according to the "Refresh rate" metadata field.

**Date range:** Requests created from January 1, 2016 through January 1, 2017, based on the `createddate` filter. The upper bound is inclusive, so requests timestamped exactly at 2017-01-01T00:00:00 are also included.

**Closed date fields:**
- `closeddate` (display name "ClosedDate"): The page describes it as "Date the request was closed. Not all request types use this field."
- `status`: Includes a "Closed" value, which indicates the request was completed.
- `servicedate` is not a closed date. It is the scheduled service date for Sanitation service types.

**Other notes:**
- The dataset is a filtered view. It includes only 12 request types, such as Graffiti Removal, Bulky Items, Illegal Dumping Pickup, and Single Streetlight Issue, so it does not cover all MyLA311 requests.
- The page does not mention newer or other yearly MyLA311 datasets. Check the MyLA311 portal or the City of Los Angeles Information Technology Agency for those.
- The license is CC0 (public domain dedication), and the data owner is listed as the Information Technology department.

The search didn't return any data.lacity.org or MyLA311 pages, so I couldn't confirm the Socrata dataset, its 2025 fields, or how closed dates are recorded.

The closest hit is an ArcGIS service titled "311 Customer Service Requests 2025." It describes 2025 calendar-year 311 requests, is updated daily, and displays dates and times in Eastern Time minus four hours. Its coordinates (about -77.0 longitude, 39.2 latitude) point to Baltimore, not Los Angeles, so it probably isn't LA's data.

Other results were from other cities: Pittsburgh's data dictionary (where closed_date_utc is the UTC time the parent ticket closed), Baton Rouge's ArcGIS layers, St. Louis, Lowell, Boston, and Montreal. They may help if you need a closed-date field definition as a reference, but none are LA sources.

To find the LA dataset, try searching for the exact title on data.lacity.org or the MyLA311 open data page, and check the closed-date field name in its data dictionary.

I ran one search. The results confirm the core facts, though none of them is a current official dataset page with a verified update date.

- **Update cadence:** The Houston 311 layer metadata says the data is refreshed monthly from the LAGAN case-management system. That's the only update-frequency detail I found. The city's 311 page separately notes a nightly-updated "current data" link, which is a different feed. (Monthly update from Lagan; Current Data (updated nightly))
- **Scope:** The dataset includes publicly available requests filed in LAGAN. Animal-related (BARC) requests are excluded because they live in a separate system, so the city suggests pairing it with a BARC location dataset for a fuller picture. (All publicly available service requests filed in the LAGAN are included in this dataset. This dataset does not include tickets for BARC; This data set can be used in conjunction with PUBLIC_BARC_Location)
- **Fields:** The layers include case number, location, council district, neighborhood, service area, department, and division, among others. (Max Record Count: 2000; Supported query Formats: JSON)
- **Hosting:** Dataset layers appear both on the city's own ArcGIS server (an archived-cases layer, with JSON, GeoJSON, and PBF query formats) and on ArcGIS Online-hosted feature services, including the Memorial Day and Tax Day flood-related 311 services. I did not confirm which is the canonical "Hub" entry. (Geometry Type: esriGeometryPoint; TaxDayFlood311_SZ (FeatureServer))
- **Coordinates:** The x,y coordinates use the NAD 1983 StatePlane Texas South Central (feet) projection, so they need reprojecting for web mapping. (NAD_1983_StatePlane_Texas_South_Central_FIPS_4204_Feet)
- **Context:** A December 2025 ABC13 report described a city dashboard that grades service categories by opening and closing request data, though it didn't say which dataset feeds it. (According to a dashboard that compiles a list of services based on opening and closing service requests)

Gaps: I did not find the current Houston Open Data Portal listing or an explicit update-date stamp. Check the city's open data portal and the layer's metadata directly before relying on the monthly schedule.

content.text:
I confirmed four of the six cities. Los Angeles and Houston are only partly resolved, and I haven't verified them.

| City | Dataset and URL | Platform | Update frequency (as stated) | Earliest record | Closure field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NYC** | 311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present, `erm2-nwe9`: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/erm2-nwe9 | Socrata | "updated daily" | 2020 | `closed_date` |
| **Chicago** | 311 Service Requests, `v6vf-nfxy`: https://data.cityofchicago.org/d/v6vf-nfxy | Socrata | "updated multiple times per day" | 2018 (new system launched 12/18/2018, plus some legacy records) | `closed_date` |
| **San Francisco** | 311 Cases, `vw6y-z8j6`: https://data.sf.gov/d/vw6y-z8j6 | Socrata | "Multiple times per hour" data change, "Daily" publishing, nightly load | 2008 (cases created since 7/1/2008) | `closed_date` |
| **Philadelphia** | 311 Service and Information Requests: https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/ | CKAN-style catalog (OpenDataPhilly) with data served from the CARTO SQL API (`public_cases_fc`) | "Updated daily" | 2014 (since Dec 8, 2014) | `closed_datetime` |
| **Los Angeles** | MyLA311 Service Request Data 2016, `ndkd-k878`: https://data.lacity.org/d/ndkd-k878 | Socrata | "Weekly" (refresh rate field) | 2016 for this dataset | `closeddate` (shown as "ClosedDate") |
| **Houston** | Houston311_Service_Requests layer in `311_ARCHIVED_CASES`: https://mycity2.houstontx.gov/pubgis01/rest/services/311/311_ARCHIVED_CASES/MapServer/0 | ArcGIS REST (city GIS server). The data.houstontx.gov portal is CKAN but has no 311 request dataset. | "Monthly update from Lagan" | Not found | Not found |

**Caveats**
- **NYC:** The 2010–2019 records are in a separate dataset, so 2020 is the earliest year for this one dataset. The "2010 to Present" version I remembered has been replaced.
- **Philadelphia:** The portal page doesn't list field names. I got `closed_datetime` by querying one row from the CARTO API, so it comes from the actual data rather than documentation. Philadelphia's data.gov listing is the only source for a daily refresh interval, and the portal page also says daily.
- **Los Angeles:**
  - The `ndkd-k878` dataset covers 2016 only and only 12 request types. I couldn't find the current all-years MyLA311 dataset: the Socrata catalog search for data.lacity.org returned only archived items.
  - LA publishes by year, so `closeddate` is probably the same in other years, but I didn't check that. LA's current 311 data may sit on a newer portal or in separate yearly datasets that I didn't locate.
- **Houston:**
  - The ArcGIS server was down during my checks ("not started" and "could not access any server machines"). I couldn't read the field list or date range. Don't rely on a guessed field name.
  - Animal (BARC) requests are excluded from this layer.
  - The city's own 311 page also mentions a nightly-updated "current data" feed that I didn't locate.

Sources:
- [NYC dataset metadata](https://data.cityofnewyork.us/api/views/erm2-nwe9.json)
- [Chicago dataset metadata](https://data.cityofchicago.org/api/views/v6vf-nfxy.json)
- [SF dataset metadata](https://data.sf.gov/api/views/vw6y-z8j6.json)
- [LA MyLA311 2016 metadata](https://data.lacity.org/api/views/ndkd-k878.json)
- [OpenDataPhilly 311 page](https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/)
- [Philadelphia CARTO API query](https://phl.carto.com/api/v2/sql?q=SELECT%20*%20FROM%20public_cases_fc%20LIMIT%201)
- [Houston 311 archived cases layer](https://mycity2.houstontx.gov/pubgis01/rest/services/311/311_ARCHIVED_CASES/MapServer/0)
- [Houston open data portal](https://data.houstontx.gov/)
